correctness.rationale: The actual rates give the canonical product weight ratio w_(a+1)/w_a=t^(a-1)[K-a]_t/[a+1]_t. On a ring the imbalance is the telescoping gradient (1-q)[K]_t([b]_t-[a]_t), proving invariance, and the one-site partition function is F(y)=t product_{j=-1}^{K-2}(1+t^j y). Its fugacity logarithmic derivative yields rho and mu=[K]_t y/(t+y), so the L-first thermodynamic flux is (1-q)mu([K]_t-mu). The canonical-to-grand-canonical limit needs the standard positive finite-support span-one local CLT at each interior density. Riemann-sum inversion for t_K=exp(lambda/K), rho=Ku yields J=(1-q)(exp(lambda*u)-1)(exp(lambda)-exp(lambda*u))/lambda², lambda=0 continuous quadratic case. Differentiating twice yields sign of 1+exp(lambda)-4exp(lambda*u), with interior sign change exactly |lambda|>log 3; strict concavity holds at equality (zero only at boundary). Independent exact rational computation confirmed F(y) and mu for 45 triples, finite-ring stationarity for L=3,4 and K=2, and finite-difference curvature for 15 settings. This is iterated L then K only, not hydrodynamic convergence.
